cards.back: The study of living organisms and their interactions with each other and their environment
The basic unit of life and the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes
All living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and all cells come from pre-existing cells
A cell without a nucleus or membrane-bound organelles
A cell with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
The control center of the cell that contains genetic material
The gel-like substance that fills the cell and contains organelles
A thin barrier that surrounds the cell and controls what enters and exits
A rigid outer layer that provides support and protection (found in plants)
Organelles that produce energy for the cell through cellular respiration
Organelles that capture light energy and convert it to chemical energy (found in plants)
Deoxyribonucleic acid - the genetic material that carries hereditary information
Ribonucleic acid - a molecule that helps in protein synthesis
A segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein or trait
A structure made of DNA and proteins that carries genetic information
Cell division that produces two identical daughter cells
Cell division that produces four genetically different cells (for reproduction)
The process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy
The process by which cells break down glucose to produce energy
The maintenance of a stable internal environment despite external changes
The framework of bones that provides support, protection, and movement
The system of muscles that enables movement and maintains posture
The system that transports blood, nutrients, and oxygen throughout the body
The system that brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide
The system that breaks down food and absorbs nutrients
The system that coordinates body activities and responds to stimuli
The system of glands that produce hormones to regulate body functions
The system that protects the body from disease and infection
The system that includes skin, hair, and nails for protection
The system that removes waste products from the blood
The system responsible for producing offspring
A muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body
Organs that exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide with the environment
The control center of the nervous system that processes information
An organ that processes nutrients, filters blood, and produces bile
Organs that filter blood and remove waste products
An organ that breaks down food with acid and enzymes
An organ where most nutrient absorption occurs
